units.translation: time. Timaeus says that six hundred years after the Trojan War, Chersicrates, a descendant of the Bacchiads, settled the island (fg 53 M. I 203): 'The Colchians crossed to the nearby island and then rushed to the Ceraunian Mountains, and they were settled among the Abantes, Nestaeans, and Oricum; the leader of the colony of the Bacchiads was Chersicrates, who was deprived of his honors by the Corinthians.'

1217-19a. And there the Fates: Timonax in the first book of his Scythica (fg 2 M. IV 522) says that in Colchis Jason married Medea, Aeetes having betrothed her to him. The same author says: 'Along the coast inside the Pontus are shown certain gardens called Jason's, where he made his landings, and in Aea gymnasia and discus grounds, and the chamber of Medea, where she was once married, and near the city a temple founded by Jason, and in addition many sanctuaries.'

b. annual sacrifices: Timaeus (fg 7 M. I 194) records concerning the sacrifice, saying that even now it is held annually, Medea having first sacrificed in the temple of Apollo; and he says that they set up altars as memorials of the marriage near the sea, not far from the city; and they call one the altar of the Nymphs, the other of the Nereids. Apollonius, however, says that one of the altars is of the Nymphs, the other of the Fates.
c. sacrifices: incense offerings. Gᵐ
d. annual: yearly. Lᵍ (P)
e. Nomios: because the judgment of Alcinous took place according to law, for this reason Medea founded a temple of Apollo Nomios.
1226. fated: allotted. Gᴳ
1235. Syrtis: there are two Syrtes in Libya. They are muddy, and ebb tides occur in them as in the ocean. They are places where sailors are dragged down and destroyed.
1237a. shoal: muddy place. Lᴳ P
b. mossy: overgrown. Lᴳ P
1238. deaf: motionless, because it is muddy.
1239. misty: we call everything abundant and copious 'misty'. Lᵐ P
1243a. pushed: thrust. Lᴳ
b. very quickly: the reading 'to be driven' is found. F
1247. watering-place: drinking-place. L Gᴳ (P)
1248. path: walk. Lᴳ (P)
1258. far-stretching: dark. Or 'far-stretching' meaning 'extending far'. Lᵐ (P)
1260. steersman: pilot. Lᴳ P
1264. shoaly: muddy. A shoal is properly land having surface water, or muddy water.
1270. brine: flood-tide. Sᵐ
1271. as much as: a little. Sᴳ
1279. was chilled: meaning 'was frozen', 'was grieved'; the figure is taken from frost.

1284. Or when the wooden images of themselves flow: whenever something terrible is about to happen, the statues are accustomed to sweat, as also in Thebes, when the war around Chaeronea was being waged by Philip against the Thebans.
1285. and lowings in the sanctuaries: and sounds in the temples produce an apparition and belief; or when lowings seem to occur around the statues.
